crime: {WITCH_NAME} had been ill again and again as a child. Each time a doctor called her cured, the illness returned by the next winter. In prison, another girl told her that those bad days had only been in her head and were over now.

Stormtide came on a fixed cycle that only {WITCH_NAME} could read in advance and could not alter. Between surges, she was mild. Two days before the next one, she signed out the whetstone in the tool log and sharpened a blade.
The other girl announced in the lounge that Stormtide was nonsense. When the hour came, she would sit alone in the cell corridor for the full hour and prove it.

At nine that night, the pressure of Stormtide made the nearby girls' heads ache and their skin crawl. As always, they left the wing. The pressure affected living people only: it could drive them away, but it could not injure them or affect objects or iron. The girl who had challenged her endured the pain and stayed in the corridor. {WITCH_NAME} approached the girl, killed her with the sharpened blade, and walked out. When the pressure faded, the others returned to find the body with a clean blade wound and no witness nearby.

At the trial, the first question was why the entire wing had emptied for that one hour. Its occupants always left on her storm days, but only {WITCH_NAME} could know their dates in advance. The tool log showed that she had prepared the blade two days before this one. The girl's promise to remain was public; the private calendar was what let her reserve an hour without witnesses.
fields.epitaph: She had marked every storm but the one that closed around her.
execution: Heavy iron presses surround her and move inward one notch at the end of each fixed interval. She can neither foresee nor alter their cycle.
Her anger cannot drive iron back. The presses close against her chest and back, then continue inward. Her ribs and breastbone break between them, and the pressure stops her breathing.

magic.name: Stormtide
magic.text: She can drive everyone nearby away with a surge of anger.
